claim: Every model scored higher on focused input (about 300 tokens) than on full input (about 113k tokens) (L2-12, L2-11, L3-12).
One distractor lowered scores, and information in the middle of a long input is used worse (L2-12, L2-11, L3-12).
With a human reference the judge reached 0.83 on items it had itself got wrong, against 0.30 without one (L3-11).
Fresh-context reviewers avoid the writer's context rot (L2-10).
Checks work when they use something outside the draft and fail when the model re-reads its own work (L1-12).
A self-written reference repeated the judge's mistakes: 0.16 when the judge was wrong, against 0.83 with a human reference (L3-11, L1-14, L3-09).
Errors correlate within a provider, and self-preference persists after labels are removed (L3-11, L1-14, L3-09).
A summarising middle step recovered far less than full disclosure: 0.241 against 0.926 (L1-07).
Packing knowledge compresses away caveats and the artifact trail unless they are typed fields (L1-08, L1-09, L2-15).
Anchoring and sycophancy survive prompt fixes and need neutral, question-form briefs (L3-07, L3-08).
Filling the window has diminishing or negative returns past a point (L2-11, L3-12).
Multi-agent research used about 15x the tokens of chat (risk row 12 of the attack).

Proposed change for risk row 1: replace the 95% sample gate with a script and checker that check every card cited in pack.md conclusions and review.json, and make the sample failure rate a ledger measure.

Proposed change for risk row 2: the coordinator writes all seven question lists and approach ids in one file before wave 1, the owner approves at the first gate, and children never see the direction file.

Proposed change for risk row 3: a second expert is a fresh reviewer on the same frozen pack, from a different model family where available; disagreement marks a claim weak and agreement never raises one.

Proposed change for risk row 4: review.json keyed by approach id and measure, a synthesis script listing disagreements, and the schemas, check and synthesis scripts run on the pilot field before wave 1.
Proposed change for risk row 5: readers hold no write or shell tools and return cards as their result, the schema rejects text outside card fields, and a quote is at most 15 words.
Proposed change for risk row 6: each session writes its ledger lines in its own folder merged by script, each child runs in its own git worktree, and the source register is deleted.

Proposed change for risk row 7: delete the source register, take field boundaries from coordinator-written question lists, and count duplicate citation ids across cards.jsonl files as a ledger measure.
Proposed change for risk row 8: make the total cap the admission rule of row 14, and state whether the coordinator is a fourth process or waves hold two children.
Proposed change for risk row 9: one background watcher script per wave writes status.json and exits on the first event, and the coordinator stops a stalled session before replacing it.
Proposed change for risk row 10: one restart path, a fresh session reading the frozen pack and must-read sections, marked 'from pack' in the ledger; without a pack, restart from cards.jsonl.
Proposed change for risk row 11: the problem sheet becomes a leaf session, gate A coverage becomes a script over question ids, and hand-over state is the watcher's status.json.
Proposed change for risk row 12: review in a fresh session from the frozen pack, delete the 60,000 token floor on the pack, and let each reader take several sub-questions in one window.

Proposed change for risk row 13: delete the self-written probe and certify an expert by four checks: coverage of coordinator-written question ids, reviewer input manifest, every cited card confirmed, and vendor or single-study verdicts marked as judgment.

Proposed change for risk row 14: the measurement field is the pilot, tokens are counted from session transcripts by script, and a wave starts only if the remaining budget covers its fields at the pilot's measured cost per field.

Ranked change 1: every review by a fresh session from the frozen pack and must-read sections, covering ceiling, crash, repair, second expert and methodologist's late review; cost is one more session start per field and a risk the pack loses caveats.
note: The file says it needs the owner's word and reverses part of amendment 1.

claim: Ranked change 2: delete the self-written probe and the 95% sample gate and check every card cited in pack.md and review.json, at a cost of one checker pass after each review.

Ranked change 3: the coordinator writes all seven question lists and approach ids before wave 1, gate A coverage becomes a script, and the problem sheet becomes a leaf session with sinks labelled 'one repository'.
Ranked change 4: delete the shared source register, merge per-session ledgers by script, take token counts from transcripts, and give each child one git worktree.
Ranked change 5: one watcher script per wave replaces the heartbeat, the PC-awake rule, 'reported' and the per-wave usage read; whether a background process can hold the PC awake is open.

Ranked change 6: one admission rule (a wave starts only if the remaining cap covers its fields at the pilot's measured cost per field), with the half/quarter split and per-pack and per-expert ceilings deleted.
Ranked change 7: the measurement field is the pilot, with a single-session control on the same field at equal budget and checks, score fixed beforehand; cost is one extra field run.
Ranked change 8: the second expert is a second fresh reviewer from the same frozen pack, different model family where available; cost is the loss of independent research, the owner's call.
Ranked change 9: aim the one refuter at every dismissal verdict on a family and every dropped field, not the three strongest leads.
note: The file gives the basis as argument_only.

claim: Ranked change 10: delete the B+ tree bullets 'balanced', 'inner nodes hold keys' and 'split on overflow', cut an over-limit pack to its limit with the rest under 'not covered', and delete the 60,000 floor.
Ranked change 11: the card evidence field becomes an enum (replicated, independent, single-study, vendor's own), and verdicts resting only on vendor or single-study cards are marked as judgment.
note: The file also leaves out logging every search query.

claim: Ranked change 12: readers take several sub-questions each with no write or shell tools, cards are returned as the result, and the pilot records one reader's first-call context.
note: The file leaves open whether the prefix is mostly tool schemas.

claim: New risk: a dismissed lead or dropped field is never challenged; severity high, basis argument_only, handled by aiming the one refuter at every dismissal and dropped field.
New risk: search ranking and vendor reports decide what the expert knows; severity medium, basis both, handled by an evidence enum and earlier research files in the seed list.
New risk: a correct card is applied outside its conditions; severity medium, basis both, handled by a checker that judges condition fit.
New risk: the tree may not beat one session at the same budget; severity medium, basis checked_source, handled by a single-session control on the pilot field.
New risk: a child is busy but not progressing; severity medium, basis checked_source, handled by a watcher that exits when no new confirmed card or file appears within the time box.

New risk: the checker and the checked share blind spots where the check is a judgment; severity low, basis checked_source, handled by grounding checks in quoted source passages and a different model family for judgments.

The original design delivers source cards with number, baseline, conditions, limits and a quote, a checker that drops failing cards, a review form citing each factual sentence, the work as files, and a fixed list of review inputs.

The owner's requirement is met if a fresh session reads only the frozen, checked pack, the must-read originals and the fixed review files, with its input manifest checked by script and its expertise certified by question-id coverage and an outside card check rather than a self-quiz.
